newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia court rules state election void.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia court rules state election void.

text.p: A Malaysian court has ruled the election for a state seat in the Eastern Malaysian state of Sarawak null and void, newspapers reported on Friday.
A High Court judge ruled on Thursday that the winning candidate had won because of "extensive bribery", The Star newspaper said.
The election, on September 8 and 9, 1996, returned the ruling Barisan Nasional (National Front) coalition candidate.
Justice Ian H.C. Chin ruled that the candidate, Mong ak Dagang, was not duly elected, saying there was no room left for any argument that bribery was not extensively prevalent, said The Star.
The losing candidate, Donald Lawan, had alleged that Mong won the election after spending more than the 30,000 ringgit (US$12,075) ceiling during the polls.
The Malaysian government has been trying to eradicate what it calls "money politics" by keeping strict checks on candidates who spend large amounts of money on electioneering.
